instruction: This quantified CAD optimization is performed in FreeCAD. Launch FreeCAD from `/usr/bin/freecad` and open `baseline.stl` there. Open /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl and /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf in FreeCAD, use them as the starting geometry and footprint guide, and redesign the part as a lightweight load-bearing fixture. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: DIN rail equipment shelf. Objective: Maximize support proxy per volume for a DIN rail equipment shelf carrying an offset load. Required output: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl. Hard constraints: keep the STL within envelope [120.0, 50.0, 42.0] mm, keep bounding-box spans at least [112.0, 44.0, 22.0] mm, keep volume between 15000.0 and 90000.0 mm^3, and preserve at least 95% sampled material coverage in every support/load prism marked in /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf and fully specified in /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json (support prisms extend from z=0 to 14.0 mm; load prisms extend from z=0 to 18.0 mm). The optimized STL must be one connected, watertight, consistently oriented solid. The evaluator parses only the real optimized.stl geometry, computes three-dimensional required-zone coverage and this continuous metric: offset shelf support proxy / volume; x-span and vertical depth matter more than unused width. It writes score.json and quant_metrics.json, and ignores any score stated in the submission. Use only the supplied task inputs and do not use evaluator-generated artifacts or evaluator implementation files.

metric.name: offset shelf support proxy per volume
